procedural_matters: FRA 19 was represented by Mathilde Lovadina (Helm).
FRA 63 was represented by Manon Peyre (Helm).
Freya Black (Helm of GBR 24) gave evidence as a witness for FRA 19.
Cxema Pico (International Jury) presented video evidence.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: At the time of the incident there was 6-7 knots of wind and flat water.
FRA 19 on starboard tack was approaching mark 1, 1.5 boat lengths clear ahead of FRA 63 and overlapped outside of another boat.
FRA 19 rounded the mark keeping a distance of about 1/2 a boat length from the inside overlapped boat.
When she gybed, she was 2.5 boat lengths from the mark.
Immediately after this, FRA 63 gybed within 0.5 metres of the mark and becoming overlapped bow to bow and 1 boat length to windward of FRA 19.
Both boats continued sailing parallel to each other, for 2 to 3 boat lengths, with FRA 63 slowly overtaking FRA 19.
FRA 19 luffed and immediately after FRA 63 started luffing.

Both boats converged for about 2 boat lengths, and when the boats were 0.5 boat lengths apart with FRA 63 1/2 a boat length bow forward and both boats with the gennakers luffing, FRA 19 started heeling to windward, putting the windward wing in the water, and began to bear away.
There was no contact and no boat took a penalty.
conclusions: By keeping clear FRA 63 complied with her obligations under rule 11 and broke no rule.
